therefore gives, with a single model, states in which part of the structure is inactive. Section
13.5 gives an example (beam cast on a prop that is added, then removed).

## 9.3 Global activation outside staged construction

Syntax

```python
m.set_active(bars=None, supports=None)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bars` | — | None | active bars; None: all |
| `supports` | — | None | nodes whose supports are active; None: all |

The subsequent analyses (static, modes, buckling, spectra…) see only the active bars and
supports. Loads and added masses carried by inactive bars are ignored; a node that is no longer
connected to any element is held fixed. `m.set_active()` restores the complete
structure. The staged construction analysis also starts from the active structure: the deactivated
bars and supports are absent from it, and its own activation keys apply to what remains.

Example `examples/manual/ex_activation.py`

```python
# Global activation: the same structure analysed with and without its intermediate support.
import keta

L, q = 6.0, 10e3
m = keta.Model()
n = [m.add_node(L * i, 0, 0) for i in range(3)]
s = m.add_section("IPE450")
b = [m.add_beam(n[i], n[i + 1], s, m.steel()) for i in range(2)]
m.add_support(n[0], dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True, rz=True)
m.add_support(n[1], dz=True)
m.add_support(n[2], dy=True, dz=True, rz=True)
for x in b:
    m.add_udl(x, wz=-q)
r = dict(m.analyze().case(1).reactions())
print(f"continuous beam: central support {r[n[1]][2] / 1e3:.2f} kN (5qL/4 = {1.25 * q * L / 1e3:.2f})")
m.set_active(supports=[n[0], n[2]])
r = dict(m.analyze().case(1).reactions())
print(f"central support deactivated: end support {r[n[0]][2] / 1e3:.2f} kN (qL = {q * L / 1e3:.2f})")
m.set_active()                                             # back to the full structure
print("reactivated:", round(dict(m.analyze().case(1).reactions())[n[1]][2] / 1e3, 2), "kN")
```

Output

```text
continuous beam: central support 74.74 kN (5qL/4 = 75.00)
central support deactivated: end support 60.00 kN (qL = 60.00)
reactivated: 74.74 kN
```

The reaction of the central support (74.74 kN) is slightly lower than $5qL/4$: the shear
deformation of the steel section relieves the intermediate support.

# Chapter 10 Output domain

## 10.1 Output sections

The internal forces of a bar are output at **output sections** evenly distributed along
its length, ends included. Their number per bar is set when the analysis is launched by the
parameter `stations` (or `stations_per_bar`):

Syntax

```python
m.analyze(stations=11, stations_abs=None)  →  Results
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stations` | — | 11 | number of output sections per bar, ends included (11: every tenth of the length); at least 2 to obtain the ends (1: mid-length section only) |

The same parameter exists for the other static analyses (`second_order`,
`cable_static`, `analyze_link_laws`, `phased`) and for the harmonic
response. The forces at the output sections are exact for span loads (concentrated, distributed,
linearly varying): they are obtained by integration of the equilibrium of the bar from its end
forces, and not by interpolation.

Syntax

```python
case_.bar_forces(bar)  →  [(x/L, N, Vy, Vz, T, My, Mz), …]
case_.end_forces(bar)  →  [12 values]
```

`bar_forces` returns a list ordered from the origin to the end; each item gives the
relative abscissa x/L then the six forces defined in Section 3.5. To obtain the force at a precise
abscissa, the number of output sections is chosen so that it is one of them, or the bar is split at
that point.

**Note.**

The number of output sections has no influence on the accuracy of the nodal displacements
nor on that of the forces: it only sets the points where the forces are output. The maximum moment
of a bar under a point load is output only if the load is placed on an output section.

## 10.2 Stresses

The normal stress at a point (y, z) of a section is obtained from the forces by the relation
σ = N/A + My·z/Iy − Mz·y/Iz (Section 3.5). The properties A, Iy and Iz are those of the section
(given or read in the JSON model).

## 10.3 Generalised stresses

The study of a stress at a particular point (shear stress with the effect of the depth variation,
stress in a tendon, force in a fibre) often reduces to a linear combination of the forces of the
section, possibly completed by a constant:

C = cN·N + cVy·Vy + cVz·Vz + cT·T + cMy·My + cMz·Mz + c0

In Python, such a quantity is computed directly from `bar_forces`, with coefficients
that are constant or variable along the abscissa (linear, parabolic, arbitrary). It can then be
combined and enveloped like any other result (Chapter 19).

Example `examples/manual/ex_stations.py`

```python
# Result stations: subdivision of the bars, reading of the forces, stresses and
# "generalised stress" (linear combination of forces) computed in Python.
import keta

def z(x):                                         # removes the displayed negative zero
    return 0.0 if abs(x) < 1e-6 else x

L, q = 12.0, -40e3
m = keta.Model()
a, b = m.add_node(0, 0, 0), m.add_node(L, 0, 0)
beam = m.add_beam(a, b, m.add_section_rect(0.4, 1.0), m.concrete())
m.add_support(a, dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
m.add_support(b, dy=True, dz=True)
m.add_udl(beam, wz=q)
m.add_point_load(b, fx=-500e3)                    # compression of 500 kN

case_ = m.analyze(stations=7).case(1)             # 7 result stations per bar (step L/6)
A, I, v = 0.4 * 1.0, 0.4 * 1.0**3 / 12, 0.5
print("  x/L      x [m]      N [kN]    Vz [kN]    My [kN.m]  sig_bot [MPa]  sig_top [MPa]")
for x, N, Vy, Vz, T, My, Mz in case_.bar_forces(beam):
    s_bot = N / A + My * (-v) / I                 # sigma = N/A + My z / Iy
    s_top = N / A + My * (+v) / I
    print(f"{x:6.4f} {x * L:9.3f} {N / 1e3:11.2f} {z(Vz) / 1e3:10.2f} {z(My) / 1e3:12.2f} "
          f"{s_bot / 1e6:14.3f} {s_top / 1e6:14.3f}")
# generalised stress: C = 0.25 N + 0.33 My + 10 (any combination of forces)
C = [0.25 * s[1] + 0.33 * s[5] + 10.0 for s in case_.bar_forces(beam)]
print("generalised stress C(x):", " ".join(f"{c / 1e3:.2f}" for c in C), "(x 1000)")
print("end forces (local axes, 12 components):")
print(" ", " ".join(f"{f / 1e3:.1f}" for f in case_.end_forces(beam)))
```

Output

```text
  x/L      x [m]      N [kN]    Vz [kN]    My [kN.m]  sig_bot [MPa]  sig_top [MPa]
0.0000     0.000     -500.00    -240.00         0.00         -1.250         -1.250
0.1667     2.000     -500.00    -160.00      -400.00          4.750         -7.250
0.3333     4.000     -500.00     -80.00      -640.00          8.350        -10.850
0.5000     6.000     -500.00       0.00      -720.00          9.550        -12.050
0.6667     8.000     -500.00      80.00      -640.00          8.350        -10.850
0.8333    10.000     -500.00     160.00      -400.00          4.750         -7.250
1.0000    12.000     -500.00     240.00         0.00         -1.250         -1.250
generalised stress C(x): -124.99 -256.99 -336.19 -362.59 -336.19 -256.99 -124.99 (x 1000)
end forces (local axes, 12 components):
  500.0 0.0 240.0 0.0 0.0 0.0 -500.0 0.0 240.0 0.0 0.0 0.0
```

The end forces (last line) are the actions of the nodes on the bar: axial force +500 kN at the
origin (opposite to N = −500 kN) and −500 kN at the end (equal to N), vertical reactions of 240 kN
at both ends.

## 10.4 Imposed output sections and other results

Syntax

```python
m.analyze(stations=11, stations_abs={bar: [x, …]})  →  Results
case_.bar_deflections(bar)  →  [(x/L, u, v, w, θx, θy, θz), …]
case_.stresses(bar)  →  [(x/L, point, σ, τ, σ_VM), …]
case_.soil_pressure(bar)  →  [(x/L, px, py, pz, mx), …]
case_.shell_forces(shell)  →  dict(n, m, q, n_principal, m_principal)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stations_abs` | m | None | abscissae of the output sections, measured from the origin of each bar cited; the other bars keep `stations` evenly spaced sections |

`bar_deflections` gives the displacements and rotations at the output sections in the
local axes of the bar ($\theta_y = -\mathrm{d}w/\mathrm{d}x$). Being obtained by double
integration of the curvature from the displacements of the ends, they are exact between the nodes
for the usual loads. `stresses` evaluates
$\sigma = N/A + M_y z/I_y - M_z y/I_z$ at the stress points of the section (four corners and
centre of a rectangle, extreme fibres of a steel section), with an estimate of τ and the von Mises
stress. `soil_pressure` gives the reaction $p = k\,w$ of an elastic foundation.
`shell_forces` returns the forces of a shell at its centre: membrane forces
`n` = (nx, ny, nxy) in N/m, moments `m` = (mx, my, mxy) in N·m/m, shear
forces `q` = (qx, qy), and the principal values with their angle.

Example `examples/manual/ex_etude_resultats.py`

```python
# Imposed result stations, displacements, stresses and soil pressure at the result stations.
import keta

L, q = 10.0, 20e3
m = keta.Model()
a, b = m.add_node(0, 0, 0), m.add_node(L, 0, 0)
p = m.add_beam(a, b, m.add_section_rect(b=0.4, h=0.6), m.add_material(e=30e9, nu=0.2))
m.add_support(a, dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True, rz=True)
m.add_support(b, dy=True, dz=True, rz=True)
m.add_udl(p, wz=-q)
r = m.analyze(stations_abs={p: [0.0, 2.5, 5.0, 7.5, 10.0]})
case_ = r.case(1)
for (xl, N, Vy, Vz, T, My, Mz), (_, u, v, w, tx, ty, tz) in zip(case_.bar_forces(p), case_.bar_deflections(p)):
    print(f"x = {xl * L:4.1f} m: My = {My / 1e3:7.2f} kN.m (q x (L-x)/2 = {q * xl * L * (L - xl * L) / 2e3:7.2f}),"
          f" w = {w * 1e3:7.3f} mm")
for xl, point, sigma, tau, vm in case_.stresses(p):
    if abs(xl - 0.5) < 1e-9:
        print(f"midspan, point {point:>6}: sigma = {sigma / 1e6:7.3f} MPa")

# beam resting on an elastic soil, without vertical support: w = q/k and p = q
m = keta.Model()
nd = [m.add_node(2.0 * i, 0, 0) for i in range(7)]
s = m.add_section_rect(b=1.0, h=0.5)
br = [m.add_beam(nd[i], nd[i + 1], s, m.concrete()) for i in range(6)]
m.add_support(nd[0], dx=True, dy=True, rx=True, rz=True)
for x in br:
    m.set_soil(x, kfz=5e7)
    m.add_udl(x, wz=-40e3)
c = m.analyze().case(1)
print(f"settlement = {c.displacement(nd[3])[2] * 1e3:.4f} mm (q/k = {40e3 / 5e7 * 1e3:.4f})")
print("soil pressure under bar 3 [kN/m]:", [round(abs(row[3]) / 1e3, 2) for row in c.soil_pressure(br[2])])
```

Output

```text
x =  0.0 m: My =    0.00 kN.m (q x (L-x)/2 =    0.00), w =   0.000 mm
x =  2.5 m: My = -187.50 kN.m (q x (L-x)/2 =  187.50), w =  -8.665 mm
x =  5.0 m: My = -250.00 kN.m (q x (L-x)/2 =  250.00), w = -12.156 mm
x =  7.5 m: My = -187.50 kN.m (q x (L-x)/2 =  187.50), w =  -8.665 mm
x = 10.0 m: My =    0.00 kN.m (q x (L-x)/2 =    0.00), w =   0.000 mm
midspan, point   +y+z: sigma = -10.417 MPa
midspan, point   -y+z: sigma = -10.417 MPa
midspan, point   +y-z: sigma =  10.417 MPa
midspan, point   -y-z: sigma =  10.417 MPa
midspan, point center: sigma =  -0.000 MPa
settlement = -0.8000 mm (q/k = 0.8000)
soil pressure under bar 3 [kN/m]: [40.0, 40.1, 40.21, 40.32, 40.4, 40.42, 40.4, 40.32, 40.21, 40.1, 40.0]
```

The rectangular section has shear areas: the elastic foundation of these bars is therefore
represented by a cubic consistent matrix (Section 6.10). At the nodes, the settlement takes its
theoretical value $q/k$; inside the bars, the soil pressure exceeds the theoretical value
$q$ by at most 1.1 % with bars of 2 m, a deviation that decreases roughly as the square of the
length of the bars. Without shear areas or releases, the linear statics computes the same beam by the exact
solution of the beam on elastic foundation, and the pressure equals q at every section.

# Chapter 11 Fixed loads

Fixed loads comprise:

- the self-weight of the structure;

- the forces and moments applied to the nodes;

- the concentrated, uniform and linearly varying loads on the bars;

- the imposed displacements of the rigid supports;

- the uniform temperature variations and the thermal gradients of the bars;

- the surface loads distributed on bars, on shells or on continuum elements;

- the equivalent loads of the prestressing of shells (Chapter 8).

## 11.1 Load cases

All the loading methods have a parameter `case` (default 1) that designates the load
case receiving the load. A case is created at its first load; the successive loads of the same case
are added together.

Syntax

```python
m.name_case(case, name)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `case` | — | — | number of the case |
| `name` | — | — | name of the case (repeated in the representation of the results); by default “LC” followed by the number |

The cases are analysed together by `m.analyze()`; their results are read by
`r.case(number)`, and the list of their numbers, in increasing order, is
`r.case_ids`.

## 11.2 Self-weight

Syntax

```python
m.add_self_weight(case=1, factor=1.0, g=None)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `case` | — | 1 | load case |
| `factor` | — | 1 | multiplying factor |
| `g` | m/s² | None | acceleration vector (gx, gy, gz); None: (0, 0, −9.80665) |

Applies to the whole structure (bars, shells, continuum elements) the weight of its materials,
ρ·A·g per unit length for a bar. The vector applied is `factor × g`. The weight of an
offset bar acts on its offset axis and reaches the nodes through the rigid arms, with the
corresponding moment. Point masses (`add_point_mass`) also have weight: each receives the
force mass × `factor × g`; nodal mass matrices and added line masses (Section 6.12.1) have
no weight.

## 11.3 Nodal loads

Syntax

```python
m.add_point_load(node, fx=0.0, fy=0.0, fz=0.0, mx=0.0, my=0.0, mz=0.0, case=1)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | — | — | loaded node |
| `fx, fy, fz` | N | 0 | components of the force, global axes |
| `mx, my, mz` | N·m | 0 | components of the moment, global axes |
| `case` | — | 1 | load case |

## 11.4 Loads on bars

### 11.4.1 Concentrated load

Syntax

```python
m.add_bar_point_load(bar, at, fx=0.0, fy=0.0, fz=0.0, case=1, frame='global')
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bar` | — | — | loaded bar |
| `at` | — | — | relative abscissa of the point of application, from 0 (origin) to 1 (end) |
| `fx, fy, fz` | N | 0 | components of the force |
| `case` | — | 1 | load case |
| `frame` | — | 'global' | axes of the components: 'global' or 'local' |

### 11.4.2 Uniformly distributed load

Syntax

```python
m.add_udl(bar, wx=0.0, wy=0.0, wz=0.0, case=1, frame='global')
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bar` | — | — | loaded bar (over its whole length) |
| `wx, wy, wz` | N/m | 0 | intensities of the distributed load |
| `case` | — | 1 | load case |
| `frame` | — | 'global' | 'global': global components, per unit length of bar; 'local': components in the local axes; 'projected': global components per unit projected length |

### 11.4.3 Linearly varying load

Syntax

```python
m.add_linear_load(bar, w1, w2, x1=0.0, x2=1.0, case=1, frame='global')
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `w1, w2` | N/m | — | intensities (wx, wy, wz) at the start and at the end of the loaded zone |
| `x1, x2` | — | 0; 1 | relative abscissae of the start and of the end of the loaded zone |
| `case, frame` | — | 1; 'global' | as for `add_udl` |

A partial uniform load is obtained with `w1 = w2` and chosen abscissae
`x1`, `x2`; a trapezoidal load with different intensities.

**Figure 11.1** — Loads on bars

### 11.4.4 Parabolic load

Syntax

```python
m.add_parabolic_load(bar, w1, wmid, w2, x1=0.0, x2=1.0, case=1, frame='global', absolute=False)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `w1, wmid, w2` | N/m | — | intensities (wx, wy, wz) at the start, at the middle and at the end of the loaded zone; the load follows the parabola that passes through these three values |
| `x1, x2, absolute` | — or m | 0; 1; False | loaded zone, as for `add_linear_load` |
| `case, frame` | — | 1; 'global' | as for `add_udl` |

The equivalent nodal forces, the forces and the deflections at the output sections are exact in
linear statics. For a parabola that is zero at the ends of a cantilever and equal to q₀ at the
middle, the fixed-end moment is q₀L²/3 and the tip deflection 7q₀L⁴/(90EI); on a beam fixed at both
ends, the end moments are q₀L²/15. The analyses that carry only linear span loads (second order by
stability functions, large displacements, exact bar on soil, warping, influence lines, plasticity
of shells and fibres) refuse it and name it.

### 11.4.5 Axes of distributed loads

The `'global'` axes give a load per metre of bar, whatever its inclination: its
resultant is w·L. The `'local'` axes give components in the axes of the bar (a load
normal to the bar, for example). The `'projected'` axes give a load per metre of length
projected on a plane perpendicular to the direction of the load: a vertical load on a bar inclined
at an angle α to the horizontal has the resultant w·L·cos α; this is the case of snow, of the
weight of fill on a vault or of loads defined per unit area in plan.

Example `examples/manual/ex_charges_repere.py`

```python
# Distributed loads on an inclined bar: global, local and projected axes.
import math
import keta

alpha = math.radians(30)
L = 10.0
for frame in ("global", "local", "projected"):
    m = keta.Model()
    a = m.add_node(0, 0, 0)
    b = m.add_node(L * math.cos(alpha), 0, L * math.sin(alpha))
    bar = m.add_beam(a, b, m.add_section_rect(0.3, 0.6), m.concrete())
    m.add_support(a, dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
    m.add_support(b, dy=True, dz=True)
    m.add_udl(bar, wz=-10e3, frame=frame)             # 10 kN/m along -Z (or local -z)
    Fx, Fy, Fz = m.analyze().case(1).sum_reactions()
    print(f"{frame:9}: resultant of the reactions Fx = {round(Fx / 1e3, 3) + 0.0:7.3f} kN, Fz = {Fz / 1e3:7.3f} kN")
print(f"expected: global 10 L = {10 * L:.3f} kN; projected 10 L cos(alpha) = {10 * L * math.cos(alpha):.3f} kN; "
      f"local: 10 L normal to the bar")
```

Output

```text
global   : resultant of the reactions Fx =   0.000 kN, Fz = 100.000 kN
local    : resultant of the reactions Fx = -50.000 kN, Fz =  86.603 kN
projected: resultant of the reactions Fx =   0.000 kN, Fz =  86.603 kN
expected: global 10 L = 100.000 kN; projected 10 L cos(alpha) = 86.603 kN; local: 10 L normal to the bar
```

Example `examples/manual/ex_charges_barres.py`

```python
# Loads on bars: point, partial distributed (trapezoid) and named load cases.
import keta

L = 8.0
m = keta.Model()
a, b = m.add_node(0, 0, 0), m.add_node(L, 0, 0)
beam = m.add_beam(a, b, m.add_section("HEB300"), m.steel())
m.add_support(a, dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
m.add_support(b, dy=True, dz=True)

m.add_bar_point_load(beam, at=0.25, fz=-40e3, case=1)                   # 40 kN at quarter span
m.add_linear_load(beam, w1=(0, 0, 0), w2=(0, 0, -30e3), x1=0.5, x2=1.0, case=2)   # triangle
m.add_udl(beam, wz=-5e3, case=3)
m.add_point_load(b, my=20e3, case=4)                                    # moment on a support
for c, name in [(1, "point"), (2, "triangle"), (3, "uniform"), (4, "moment")]:
    m.name_case(c, name)

r = m.analyze(stations=17)
print("cases:", r.case_ids, "-", r.case(1))
for c in r.case_ids:
    case_ = r.case(c)
    Ra, Rb = (rz[2] for _, rz in case_.reactions())
    Mmax = max(case_.bar_forces(beam), key=lambda s: abs(s[5]))
    print(f"{c} RA = {Ra / 1e3:7.3f} kN  RB = {Rb / 1e3:7.3f} kN  "
          f"|M|max = {abs(Mmax[5]) / 1e3:7.3f} kN.m at x/L = {Mmax[0]:.4f}")
# Checks: RA(1) = 3P/4; triangle from 0.5L to L: R = 30 x 4 / 2 = 60 kN at 2/3 of [4, 8] m
assert abs(dict(r.case(1).reactions())[a][2] - 30e3) < 1e-6
assert abs(dict(r.case(2).reactions())[b][2] - 60e3 * (4 + 8 / 3) / 8) < 1e-6
```

Output

```text
cases: [1, 2, 3, 4] - <keta.CaseResult 'point': 2 nodes, 1 bars>
1 RA =  30.000 kN  RB =  10.000 kN  |M|max =  60.000 kN.m at x/L = 0.2500
2 RA =  10.000 kN  RB =  50.000 kN  |M|max =  50.781 kN.m at x/L = 0.6875
3 RA =  20.000 kN  RB =  20.000 kN  |M|max =  40.000 kN.m at x/L = 0.5000
4 RA =  -2.500 kN  RB =   2.500 kN  |M|max =  20.000 kN.m at x/L = 1.0000
```

Under the triangular load, the largest moment at the output sections (50.78 kN·m, at
x/L = 0.6875 with 17 output sections) is slightly below the maximum of the span (50.89 kN·m at
x/L = 0.704, between two output sections): the forces are output only at the output sections.

### 11.4.6 Moments, partial loads and absolute abscissae

Syntax

```python
m.add_udl(bar, wx=0, wy=0, wz=0, case=1, frame='global', mx=0, my=0, mz=0, x1=None, x2=None, absolute=False)
m.add_linear_load(bar, w1, w2, x1=0, x2=1, case=1, frame='global', m1=None, m2=None, absolute=False)
m.add_bar_point_load(bar, at, fx=0, fy=0, fz=0, case=1, frame='global', mx=0, my=0, mz=0, absolute=False)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mx, my, mz` | N·m/m or N·m | 0 | distributed moment (distributed loads) or concentrated moment (point load) |
| `m1, m2` | N·m/m | None | distributed moment varying linearly from x1 to x2 |
| `x1, x2` | — or m | None | loaded extent of a uniform load (by default: the whole bar) |
| `absolute` | — | False | abscissae in metres from the origin of the bar instead of fractions of its length |

Example `examples/manual/ex_charges_couples.py`

```python
# Moments on bars, partial loads and absolute abscissae.
import keta

L = 10.0
m = keta.Model()
a, b = m.add_node(0, 0, 0), m.add_node(L, 0, 0)
p = m.add_beam(a, b, m.add_section("IPE400"), m.steel())
m.add_support(a, dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True, rz=True)
m.add_support(b, dy=True, dz=True, rz=True)
m.add_bar_point_load(p, 0.5, my=50e3, frame="local", case=1)              # 50 kN.m moment at midspan
m.add_udl(p, my=3e3, frame="local", case=2)                                # distributed moment of 3 kN.m/m
m.add_udl(p, wz=-10e3, x1=0.0, x2=4.0, absolute=True, case=3)              # 10 kN/m over the first 4 metres
m.add_bar_point_load(p, 2.5, fz=-20e3, absolute=True, case=4)              # 20 kN at 2.5 m from the start
r = m.analyze()
for k, expected in ((1, 50e3 / L), (2, 3e3), (3, 10e3 * 4 * (L - 2) / L), (4, 20e3 * (L - 2.5) / L)):
    ra = dict(r.case(k).reactions())[a][2]
    print(f"case {k}: reaction at A = {ra / 1e3:8.3f} kN (by hand, absolute value: {expected / 1e3:6.3f})")
```

Output

```text
case 1: reaction at A =   -5.000 kN (by hand, absolute value:  5.000)
case 2: reaction at A =   -3.000 kN (by hand, absolute value:  3.000)
case 3: reaction at A =   32.000 kN (by hand, absolute value: 32.000)
case 4: reaction at A =   15.000 kN (by hand, absolute value: 15.000)
```

## 11.5 Imposed support displacements

Syntax

```python
m.add_support_disp(node, dx=None, dy=None, dz=None, rx=None, ry=None, rz=None, case=1)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | — | — | supported node |
| `dx, dy, dz` | m | None | imposed translations (global axes) |
| `rx, ry, rz` | rad | None | imposed rotations |
| `case` | — | 1 | load case |

**Important.**

A displacement can be imposed only on a component rigidly restrained by a support. The
component must therefore have been declared by `fix`, `pin` or
`add_support`.

Example `examples/manual/ex_tassement.py`

```python
# Imposed support displacement: continuous beam on three supports, settlement of 10 mm of the central support.
import keta

L, EI, d = 6.0, 30e9 * 4.0e-3, -0.010
m = keta.Model()
n = [m.add_node(L * i, 0, 0) for i in range(3)]
sec = m.add_section_props(sx=0.2, iy=4.0e-3, iz=1e-3, ix=1e-3)
b = [m.add_beam(n[i], n[i + 1], sec, m.add_material(30e9, 0.2)) for i in range(2)]
m.add_support(n[0], dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
m.add_support(n[1], dy=True, dz=True)
m.add_support(n[2], dy=True, dz=True)
m.add_support_disp(n[1], dz=d, case=1)
case_ = m.analyze().case(1)
M = case_.bar_forces(b[0])[-1][5]
R = dict(case_.reactions())[n[1]][2]
print(f"imposed displacement: {case_.displacement(n[1])[2] * 1e3:.3f} mm")
print(f"moment over the central support: {M / 1e3:.3f} kN.m (-3 EI |d| / L² = {-3 * EI * -d / L**2 / 1e3:.3f} kN.m, bottom fibre in tension)")
print(f"reaction of the central support: {R / 1e3:.3f} kN (-6 EI |d| / L³ = {-6 * EI * -d / L**3 / 1e3:.3f} kN)")
```

Output

```text
imposed displacement: -10.000 mm
moment over the central support: -100.000 kN.m (-3 EI |d| / L² = -100.000 kN.m, bottom fibre in tension)
reaction of the central support: -33.333 kN (-6 EI |d| / L³ = -33.333 kN)
```

## 11.6 Thermal actions

Syntax

```python
m.add_thermal(bar, dt, gy=0.0, gz=0.0, case=1)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bar` | — | — | loaded bar |
| `dt` | K | — | uniform temperature variation |
| `gy, gz` | K/m | 0 | temperature gradients along the local axes y and z (dT/dy, dT/dz) |
| `case` | — | 1 | load case |

The uniform variation produces a free expansion α·ΔT; a gradient produces a free curvature
α·g. For a bar of depth h whose top fibre (z = +h/2) is warmer by Δθ than the bottom fibre,
`gz = Δθ / h`. The material must have a coefficient of thermal expansion
(`alpha_temp`, Chapter 7).

Example `examples/manual/ex_temperature.py`

```python
# Thermal actions: uniform variation on a bar clamped at both ends, gradient on a cantilever.
import keta

E, alpha, A, h = 210e9, 1.2e-5, 0.02, 0.5
m = keta.Model()
steel = m.add_material(e=E, nu=0.3, alpha_temp=alpha)
sec = m.add_section_props(sx=A, iy=8e-4, iz=2e-4, ix=1e-4)
a, b = m.add_node(0, 0, 0), m.add_node(10, 0, 0)
bar = m.add_beam(a, b, sec, steel)
m.fix(a)
m.fix(b)
m.add_thermal(bar, dt=30.0, case=1)                        # +30 K uniform
N = m.analyze().case(1).bar_forces(bar)[5][1]
print(f"fixed-fixed, +30 K: N = {N / 1e3:.3f} kN (closed form -E A alpha dT = {-E * A * alpha * 30 / 1e3:.3f} kN)")

m = keta.Model()
steel = m.add_material(e=E, nu=0.3, alpha_temp=alpha)
sec = m.add_section_props(sx=A, iy=8e-4, iz=2e-4, ix=1e-4)
a, b = m.add_node(0, 0, 0), m.add_node(10, 0, 0)
bar = m.add_beam(a, b, sec, steel)
m.fix(a)
m.add_thermal(bar, dt=0.0, gz=20.0 / h, case=1)            # 20 K difference between fibres z = -h/2 and +h/2
ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz = m.analyze().case(1).displacement(b)
k = alpha * 20.0 / h                                        # free curvature
print(f"cantilever, gradient 40 K/m: uz = {uz * 1e3:.3f} mm, ry = {ry * 1e3:.4f} mrad")
print(f"closed forms: |uz| = k L²/2 = {k * 100 / 2 * 1e3:.3f} mm, |ry| = k L = {k * 10 * 1e3:.4f} mrad")
```

Output

```text
fixed-fixed, +30 K: N = -1512.000 kN (closed form -E A alpha dT = -1512.000 kN)
cantilever, gradient 40 K/m: uz = -24.000 mm, ry = 4.8000 mrad
closed forms: |uz| = k L²/2 = 24.000 mm, |ry| = k L = 4.8000 mrad
```

## 11.7 Imposed strains

Syntax

```python
m.add_prestrain(bar, strain=0, ky=0, kz=0, case=1, kx=0)
m.add_prestrain_linear(bar, start, end, case=1, kx=(0, 0))
m.add_prestrain_parabolic(bar, start, mid, end, case=1, kx=(0, 0, 0))
m.add_prestrain_point(bar, at, dx=0, ry=0, rz=0, dy=0, dz=0, rx=0, absolute=False, case=1)
m.add_surface_thermal(slab, dt, grad=0.0, case=1)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strain` | — | 0 | imposed elongation (> 0: elongation) |
| `ky, kz` | 1/m | 0 | imposed curvatures about the local axes y and z, opposite to the rotation gradients: ky = −dθy/dx = d²w/dx² (ky > 0 elongates the −z fibre, like a thermal gradient gz = −ky/α) and kz = −dθz/dx = −d²v/dx² (kz > 0 elongates the +y fibre, like gy = kz/α) |
| `kx` | rad/m | 0; (0, 0) | imposed rate of twist dθx/dx, the free torsion of the bar (uniform, or from the origin to the end for `add_prestrain_linear`); fixed at both ends, the bar carries the torsional moment −GJ times its mean |
| `start, end` | — | — | (strain, ky, kz) at the origin and at the end: linear variation |
| `mid` | — | — | (strain, ky, kz) at the middle of the bar: the parabola passing through start, mid and end (`kx`: its three rates of twist) |
| `at` | — or m | — | position of a concentrated dislocation |
| `dx, dy, dz, rx, ry, rz` | m, rad | 0 | discontinuities of displacement and rotation between the two faces of the cut |
| `slab, dt, grad` | —, K, K/m | — | shells of the group `slab`: uniform variation and gradient through the thickness |

An imposed strain is a free strain $\varepsilon_0, \kappa_0$: on a statically determinate
structure it produces displacements without forces, on a statically indeterminate structure forces
without having to go through an equivalent temperature. It represents a differential shrinkage, a
fabrication camber, an erection misfit. The parabolic field reproduces the creep curvature
$\varphi\,M/EI$ of a bar under distributed load, whose moment is parabolic: on a statically
indeterminate structure with uniform creep, it redistributes nothing and the deflection is
multiplied by $1 + \varphi$.

Example `examples/manual/ex_deformations_imposees.py`

```python
# Imposed strains: uniform curvature, shortening, linear variation, dislocation.
import keta

E, A, I, L = 30e9, 0.2, 4e-3, 5.0
m = keta.Model()
a, b = m.add_node(0, 0, 0), m.add_node(L, 0, 0)
p = m.add_beam(a, b, m.add_section_props(sx=A, iy=I, iz=I, ix=I), m.add_material(e=E, nu=0.2))
m.fix(a)
k = 2e-4
m.add_prestrain(p, ky=k, case=1)                        # uniform curvature
m.add_prestrain(p, strain=-3e-4, case=2)                # uniform shortening
m.add_prestrain_linear(p, (0, 0, 0), (0, k, 0), case=3)  # curvature from 0 to k
m.add_prestrain_point(p, 0.5, ry=1e-3, case=4)          # 1 mrad kink at mid-length
r = m.analyze()
d = [r.case(c).displacement(b) for c in (1, 2, 3, 4)]
print(f"uniform curvature:  rotation {d[0][4] * 1e3:8.4f} mrad (kL = {k * L * 1e3:.4f}), "
      f"deflection {d[0][2] * 1e3:8.4f} mm (kL2/2 = {k * L * L / 2 * 1e3:.4f})")
print(f"shortening:         ux = {d[1][0] * 1e3:8.4f} mm (eps L = {-3e-4 * L * 1e3:.4f})")
print(f"linear curvature:   rotation {d[2][4] * 1e3:8.4f} mrad (kL/2 = {k * L / 2 * 1e3:.4f})")
print(f"kink at mid-length: deflection {d[3][2] * 1e3:8.4f} mm (1e-3 L/2 = {1e-3 * L / 2 * 1e3:.4f})")

# same strains on a bar clamped at both ends: forces, no displacement
m.fix(b)
st = m.analyze().case(2).bar_forces(p)[5]
print(f"restrained shortening: N = {st[1] / 1e3:.1f} kN (-E A eps = {E * A * 3e-4 / 1e3:.1f})")
```

Output

```text
uniform curvature:  rotation  -1.0000 mrad (kL = 1.0000), deflection   2.5000 mm (kL2/2 = 2.5000)
shortening:         ux =  -1.5000 mm (eps L = -1.5000)
linear curvature:   rotation  -0.5000 mrad (kL/2 = 0.5000)
kink at mid-length: deflection   2.5000 mm (1e-3 L/2 = 2.5000)
restrained shortening: N = 1800.0 kN (-E A eps = 1800.0)
```

## 11.8 Surface loads on bars

Syntax

```python
m.add_area_load(polygon, qx=0.0, qy=0.0, qz=0.0, mode='two_way', span=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0), case=1)  →  int
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `polygon` | m | — | vertices (x, y, z) of a convex plane panel bounded by bars |
| `qx, qy, qz` | Pa | 0 | surface load (global vector) |
| `mode` | — | 'two_way' | 'two_way': distribution to the nearest edge (45° lines); 'one_way': strips parallel to `span`, carried by the bars at the ends of the strips |
| `span` | — | (1, 0, 0) | span direction of the 'one_way' mode |
| `case` | — | 1 | load case |

The load of the panel is converted into linear loads on the bars of its boundary (tributary
area). The method returns the number of bar loads created.

## 11.9 Loads on shells

Syntax

```python
m.add_surface_pressure(slab, qx=0.0, qy=0.0, qz=0.0, frame='global', case=1)
m.add_polygon_pressure(polygon, qx=0.0, qy=0.0, qz=0.0, holes=[], slab=0, case=1)
m.add_hydrostatic(gamma, surface_point, slab=0, side=1.0, down=(0, 0, -1), case=1)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slab` | — | — / 0 | loaded group of shells (0: all the shells) |
| `qx, qy, qz` | Pa | 0 | pressure; for `add_surface_pressure` in 'normal' axes, `qz` is the pressure along the normal of each facet |
| `frame` | — | 'global' | 'global' (vector per unit area), 'normal' (along the normal), 'projected' (per unit area in plan) |
| `polygon, holes` | m | — | boundary of the loaded polygon and boundaries of the openings, in plan; the pressure is given per unit projected area |
| `gamma` | N/m³ | — | unit weight of the fluid |
| `surface_point` | m | — | a point of the free surface |
| `side` | — | 1 | +1: pressure along the normal of the facets, −1: in the opposite direction |
| `down` | — | (0, 0, −1) | direction of depth |

The hydrostatic pressure is γ times the depth below the free surface, zero above; the facets cut
by the free surface are integrated over their wetted part.

Example `examples/manual/ex_charges_surfaciques.py`

```python
# Area loads: load distribution zone on a panel of beams, polygonal
# pressure and hydrostatic pressure on shells.
import keta

# 1) Floor of 6 m x 4 m bordered by four beams: 5 kN/m2 distributed to the beams
for mode in ("two_way", "one_way"):
    m = keta.Model()
    c = [m.add_node(x, y, 0) for x, y in ((0, 0), (6, 0), (6, 4), (0, 4))]
    sec, mat = m.add_section("IPE300"), m.steel()
    beams = [m.add_beam(c[i], c[(i + 1) % 4], sec, mat) for i in range(4)]
    for nd in c:
        m.pin(nd)
    nb = m.add_area_load([(0, 0, 0), (6, 0, 0), (6, 4, 0), (0, 4, 0)], qz=-5e3, mode=mode, span=(0, 1, 0))
    case_ = m.analyze().case(1)
    M = [abs(case_.bar_forces(p)[5][5]) / 1e3 for p in beams]
    print(f"{mode:8}: {nb} bar loads, total = {case_.sum_reactions()[2] / 1e3:.2f} kN, "
          f"midspan M of the beams = {', '.join(f'{x:.2f}' for x in M)} kN.m")

# 2) Vertical wall of 3 m x 2.5 m (shells), clamped at the base, retaining 2.5 m of water
m = keta.Model()
concrete = m.add_material(e=30e9, nu=0.2)
g = [[m.add_node(0.5 * i, 0.0, 0.5 * j) for i in range(7)] for j in range(6)]
for j in range(5):
    for i in range(6):
        m.add_shell(g[j][i], g[j][i + 1], g[j + 1][i + 1], 0.25, concrete, slab=1)
        m.add_shell(g[j][i], g[j + 1][i + 1], g[j + 1][i], 0.25, concrete, slab=1)
for nd in g[0]:
    m.fix(nd)
m.add_hydrostatic(gamma=9810.0, surface_point=(0.0, 0.0, 2.5), slab=1, case=1)
Fy = m.analyze().case(1).sum_reactions()[1]
print(f"hydrostatic thrust: |Fy| = {abs(Fy) / 1e3:.3f} kN (gamma h² b / 2 = {9810 * 2.5**2 * 3 / 2 / 1e3:.3f} kN)")

# 3) Pressure on a polygon with an opening, applied in plan on a horizontal slab
m = keta.Model()
concrete = m.add_material(e=30e9, nu=0.2)
g = [[m.add_node(1.0 * i, 1.0 * j, 0.0) for i in range(7)] for j in range(5)]
for j in range(4):
    for i in range(6):
        m.add_shell(g[j][i], g[j][i + 1], g[j + 1][i + 1], 0.2, concrete, slab=1)
        m.add_shell(g[j][i], g[j + 1][i + 1], g[j + 1][i], 0.2, concrete, slab=1)
for nd in g[0] + g[-1]:
    m.pin(nd)
outline = [(0.5, 0.5, 0), (5.5, 0.5, 0), (5.5, 3.5, 0), (0.5, 3.5, 0)]
opening = [(2.0, 1.5, 0), (3.0, 1.5, 0), (3.0, 2.5, 0), (2.0, 2.5, 0)]
m.add_polygon_pressure(outline, qz=-4e3, holes=[opening], case=1)
Fz = m.analyze().case(1).sum_reactions()[2]
print(f"polygonal pressure: Fz = {Fz / 1e3:.3f} kN (4 kN/m2 x (15 - 1) m2 = 56.000 kN)")
```

Output

```text
two_way : 10 bar loads, total = 120.00 kN, midspan M of the beams = 38.33, 13.33, 38.33, 13.33 kN.m
one_way : 2 bar loads, total = 120.00 kN, midspan M of the beams = 45.00, 0.00, 45.00, 0.00 kN.m
hydrostatic thrust: |Fy| = 91.969 kN (gamma h² b / 2 = 91.969 kN)
polygonal pressure: Fz = 56.000 kN (4 kN/m2 x (15 - 1) m2 = 56.000 kN)
```

## 11.10 Loads on continuum elements

Syntax

```python
m.add_continuum_traction(element, face, traction, case=1)
m.add_continuum_pressure(element, face, p, case=1)
m.add_continuum_thermal(element, T, T0=0.0, case=1)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `element` | — | — | continuum element |
| `face` | — | — | side of a plane element (from vertex `face` to the next) or face of a hexahedron (0: bottom, 1: top, then η = −1, ξ = +1, η = +1, ξ = −1) |
| `traction` | Pa | — | vector (tx, ty, tz) of the force per unit area (per radian for an axisymmetric element) |
| `p` | Pa | — | pressure, positive when it pushes towards the inside of the element |
| `T` | K | — | nodal temperatures {node: T}, for example from `conduction` (Chapter 18) |
| `T0` | K | 0 | reference temperature |

The equivalent nodal forces are computed by integration consistent with the shape functions.
The example of Section 6.15 applies a face traction.

# Chapter 12 Live loads

## 12.1 Principle

Live loads (vehicles, convoys, distributed traffic loads, crowd) are moving: their most
unfavourable position depends on the quantity studied. keta treats them by **influence lines**
and **influence surfaces**. For a given response (displacement, reaction, force at a section),
the influence line η(s) is the value of the response when a unit load, of given direction, is at
the abscissa s of the running path. The value of a response under a set of loads Pi at
the abscissae si and of distributed loads q(s) is then:

R = Σ Pi · η(si) + ∫ q(s) · η(s) ds

The placement functions seek the position (and, for distributed loads, the extent) that makes R
maximum or minimum. All the lines are computed by the adjoint method: a single factorisation of the
structure gives the complete line.

The loads of the code models are supplied in the form of convoys, densities or wheel sets
(Sections 12.4 to 12.8); an arbitrary convoy is described directly in Python.

## 12.2 Influence lines

Syntax

```python
m.influence_line(bars, response, dir=(0, 0, -1), per_bar=11)  →  InfluenceLine
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bars` | — | — | running path: ordered list of contiguous bars; the abscissa s starts at the origin of the first bar |
| `response` | — | — | response studied, dictionary (Table 12.1) |
| `dir` | — | (0, 0, −1) | direction of the moving unit load (global axes); by default vertical downwards |
| `per_bar` | — | 11 | number of calculation points per bar |

Table 12.1 — Responses studied

| Dictionary | Response |
|---|---|
| `dict(kind='displacement', node=n, comp=c)` | displacement of node n, component c (0 to 5) |
| `dict(kind='reaction', node=n, comp=c)` | reaction of the support of node n |
| `dict(kind='bar_force', bar=b, x=x, comp=c)` | force in bar b at the distance x [m] from its origin; c = 0 to 5 for N, Vy, Vz, T, My, Mz |
| `dict(kind='bar_displacement', bar=b, x=x, comp=c)` | displacement of bar b at the distance x |

The `InfluenceLine` object returned has the following attributes and methods:

**Figure 12.1** — Influence lines of a continuous bridge of 25 + 30 + 25 m, computed by keta

| Item | Role |
|---|---|
| `s`, `eta` | abscissae [m] and ordinates (response per newton) of the points computed |
| `at(s)` | ordinate at an arbitrary point (zero outside the path) |
| `integral(a, b)` | integral of η over [a, b] |
| `integral_pos()`, `integral_neg()` | areas of the positive and negative zones |
| `zones(sign=1)` | zones of one sign: list of (start, end, area) |
| `point_extreme()` | (max, min) under a single unit load |
| `InfluenceLine.from_samples(s, eta)` | piecewise linear line defined point by point (known line, check) |

**Note.**

With the default direction (downward load) and the conventions of Chapter 3, the line of the
midspan moment of a beam is negative (span moment that puts the bottom fibre in tension) and the
line of a vertical reaction is positive. The extremes to be retained are therefore read according
to the sign: the “min” of a span moment is the usual positive moment.

## 12.3 Convoys and distributed loads

A convoy is a dictionary `dict(axles=[(offset, load), …], segments=[(start, length,
total), …])`: point axles located by their offset [m] relative to the first one, and uniform
distributed loads defined by their start, their length and their total load [N]. The functions of
the code models return this format; it can also be written directly.

Syntax

```python
keta.convoy_extreme(line, convoy, steps=500)  →  (max, min, s_max, s_min)
keta.udl_extreme(line, q)  →  (q·A⁺, q·A⁻, 0, 0)
keta.multi_vehicle_extreme(line, vehicles, udl=0.0, steps=200)  →  (max, min, positions_max, positions_min)
keta.intensity_udl_extreme(line, density, sign=1)  →  (value, loaded length, zones)
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `line` | — | — | influence line |
| `convoy` | — | — | convoy (dictionary above), run in one direction only; for the other direction, change the sign of the offsets |
| `steps` | — | 500 | number of positions tried |
| `q` | N/m | — | free distributed load, applied over all the zones of the same sign |
| `vehicles` | — | — | list of vehicles dict(axles, occ_back, occ_front, rem_back, rem_front): axles, rear and front clearances [m], and lengths over which the concomitant distributed load is removed |
| `udl` | N/m | 0 | concomitant distributed load, removed under the vehicles |
| `density` | — | — | Python function q(L) of the loaded length L [m] → density [N/m] |
| `sign` | — | 1 | sign of the loaded zones (+1 or −1) |

`convoy_extreme` slides the convoy along the line (axles outside the path have no
effect) and returns the extremes and the corresponding position of the reference of the convoy
(the point of zero offset).
`multi_vehicle_extreme` places several vehicles without overlap and gives the
optimum on the grid of positions. `intensity_udl_extreme` treats loads whose intensity
depends on the loaded length: it selects the most unfavourable subset of zones.

Example `examples/manual/ex_ligne_influence.py`

```python
# Influence lines: continuous bridge with three spans 25 + 30 + 25 m, moment over a pier
# and moment at the middle of the central span; extremes under point load, distributed load and vehicles.
import keta

spans = [25.0, 30.0, 25.0]
m = keta.Model()
xs = [0.0]
for L in spans:
    xs += [xs[-1] + L * i / 10 for i in range(1, 11)]
n = [m.add_node(x, 0, 0) for x in xs]
sec = m.add_section_props(sx=6.0, iy=4.0, iz=40.0, ix=5.0)
b = [m.add_beam(n[i], n[i + 1], sec, m.concrete()) for i in range(len(n) - 1)]
m.add_support(n[0], dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
for i in (10, 20, 30):
    m.add_support(n[i], dy=True, dz=True)

# My at the end of bar 10 (over pier 1) and at the middle of the central span (end of bar 15)
line_pier = m.influence_line(b, dict(kind="bar_force", bar=b[9], x=2.5, comp=4))
line_mid = m.influence_line(b, dict(kind="bar_force", bar=b[14], x=3.0, comp=4))
print(f"line: {len(line_pier.s)} abscissae from {line_pier.s[0]:.1f} to {line_pier.s[-1]:.1f} m")
for name, line in (("M over pier", line_pier), ("M midspan", line_mid)):
    mx, mn = line.point_extreme()
    print(f"{name:12}: unit load -> max {mx:7.3f}, min {mn:7.3f} m; "
          f"areas + {line.integral_pos():8.3f} / - {line.integral_neg():8.3f} m2")
    print(f"{'':12}  positive zones: " + ", ".join(f"[{a:.2f}; {c:.2f}]" for a, c, _ in line.zones(1)))
    print(f"{'':12}  ordinate at s = 40 m: {line.at(40.0):.4f} m")

# Moment at the middle of the central span: vehicles and distributed loads (characteristic values, N.m)
q = 9e3 * 3.0                                    # 9 kN/m2 on a lane of 3 m
cases = [("LM1 tandem lane 1", keta.convoy_extreme(line_mid, keta.lm1_tandem(1), 2000)),
         ("distributed 27 kN/m", keta.udl_extreme(line_mid, q)),
         ("LM71", keta.convoy_extreme(line_mid, keta.rail_lm71(), 2000))]
for name, (mx, mn, rmx, rmn) in cases:
    print(f"{name:19}: max = {mx / 1e3:9.1f} kN.m, min = {mn / 1e3:9.1f} kN.m")
```

Output

```text
line: 301 abscissae from 0.0 to 80.0 m
M over pier : unit load -> max   2.590, min  -0.644 m; areas +   86.579 / -  -10.463 m2
              positive zones: [0.00; 55.00]
              ordinate at s = 40 m: 2.4107 m
M midspan   : unit load -> max   0.859, min  -5.089 m; areas +   27.902 / -  -64.286 m2
              positive zones: [0.00; 25.00], [55.00; 80.00]
              ordinate at s = 40 m: -5.0893 m
LM1 tandem lane 1  : max =     514.2 kN.m, min =   -2878.0 kN.m
distributed 27 kN/m: max =     753.3 kN.m, min =   -1735.7 kN.m
LM71               : max =    1246.2 kN.m, min =   -6604.8 kN.m
```

## 12.4 Road load models of EN 1991-2

Syntax

```python
keta.en_lane_division(width)  →  (n, lane width, remaining width)
keta.lm1_tandem(rank, factors='class1')  →  convoy
keta.lm1_udl(rank, lane_width, factors='class1')  →  N/m
keta.lm1_lane_extreme(line, rank, lane_width, factors='class1', steps=500)  →  (max, min, s_max, s_min)
keta.lm2_axle(beta_q=1.0, french_na=False)  →  convoy
keta.lm2_wheels(beta_q=1.0)  →  [(dx, dy, P), …]
keta.lm4_crowd(lane_width)  →  N/m
keta.annex_a_vehicle(name, layout)  →  [(dx, dy, P), …]
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | m | — | width of the carriageway |
| `rank` | — | — | rank of the lane (1, 2, 3, …) |
| `factors` | — | 'class1' | adjustment factors α: 'class1' or 'class2' |
| `lane_width` | m | — | width of the lane |
| `beta_q` | — | 1 | factor βQ of model 2 |
| `french_na` | — | False | values of the French National Annex |
| `name` | — | — | special vehicle of Annex A: '600/150' to '3600/240/240' |
| `layout` | — | — | transverse distribution of the axle lines: [(dy, fraction), …] |

`lm1_lane_extreme` places on a lane the tandem and the distributed load of model 1 for
the extreme of an influence line. The fatigue models are supplied in the same way:

Syntax

```python
keta.flm1_tandem(lane)  →  convoy
keta.flm1_udl(lane, lane_width)  →  N/m
keta.flm2_lorry(i)  →  convoy           (frequent lorries 1 to 5)
keta.flm3_vehicle()  →  convoy
keta.flm3_double(gap=40.0)  →  convoy    (second vehicle with 36 kN axles)
keta.flm4_lorry(i)  →  convoy
keta.flm4_share(i, traffic)  →  %       (traffic: 'long', 'medium' or 'local')
```

## 12.5 Road loads of Fascicule 61 Titre II

Syntax

```python
keta.fasc61_a_of_l(loaded_length)  →  N/m²
keta.fasc61_a1(bridge_class, loaded_lanes)  →  a1
keta.fasc61_a2(bridge_class, lane_width)  →  a2
keta.fasc61_a_lane_load(loaded_length, bridge_class, lane_width)  →  N/m
keta.fasc61_bc()  →  convoy
keta.fasc61_bt()  →  convoy
keta.fasc61_mc120()  →  convoy
keta.fasc61_delta(element_length, permanent_load, max_axle_load)  →  δ
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loaded_length` | m | — | loaded length |
| `bridge_class` | — | — | class of the bridge (1, 2 or 3) |
| `loaded_lanes` | — | — | number of loaded lanes |
| `element_length` | m | — | length of the element for the dynamic amplification factor |
| `permanent_load` | N | — | permanent load of the element |
| `max_axle_load` | N | — | maximum load of the axles that can be placed on it |

`fasc61_a_lane_load` gives the load per metre of a lane of given width,
a2 · max(a1·A(l), 400 − 0.2·l kg/m²) × width, a1 being that of one loaded lane; combined with
`intensity_udl_extreme`, it leads to the most unfavourable loaded length. The convoys Bc
(two 30 t lorries one behind the other), Bt (one tandem of two 16 t axles) and Mc120 (110 t tracked vehicle on 6.1 m)
are given for one line of vehicles, without the bc or bt factor and without dynamic amplification:
these factors apply to the result.

Example `examples/manual/ex_convois.py`

```python
# Road live loads on an influence line: LM1 load model per lane,
# A(l), Bc and Mc120 systems and Courbon's transverse distribution.
import keta

# Simply supported span of 30 m: midspan moment (exact triangular line, sampled)
L = 30.0
m = keta.Model()
n = [m.add_node(L * i / 12, 0, 0) for i in range(13)]
b = [m.add_beam(n[i], n[i + 1], m.add_section_props(5.0, 3.0, 30.0, 4.0), m.concrete()) for i in range(12)]
m.add_support(n[0], dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
m.add_support(n[-1], dy=True, dz=True)
line = m.influence_line(b, dict(kind="bar_force", bar=b[5], x=2.5, comp=4), per_bar=21)
print(f"maximum ordinate |eta| = {abs(line.point_extreme()[1]):.4f} m (L/4 = {L / 4:.4f} m)")

# EN 1991-2, LM1: lanes of 3 m on a carriageway of 9 m
nl, width, rest = keta.en_lane_division(9.0)
print(f"carriageway of 9 m: {nl} lanes of {width} m, remaining area {rest} m")
for lane in (1, 2, 3):
    res = keta.lm1_lane_extreme(line, lane, width)
    print(f"lane {lane}: tandem {keta.lm1_tandem(lane)['axles'][0][1] / 1e3:.0f} kN/axle, "
          f"UDL {keta.lm1_udl(lane, width) / 1e3:.1f} kN/m -> M = {min(res[:2]) / 1e3:9.1f} kN.m")

# Fascicule 61 Titre II: A(l) on the most unfavourable loaded length, Bc, Mc120
density = lambda Lc: keta.fasc61_a_lane_load(Lc, 1, 3.5) * 2   # 2 lanes, first-class bridge [N/m]
val, Lc, zones = keta.intensity_udl_extreme(line, density, sign=-1)
print(f"A(l): loaded length {Lc:.2f} m, A(30) = {keta.fasc61_a_of_l(30.0):.1f} N/m2 -> M = {val / 1e3:.1f} kN.m")
G, S = 30 * 150e3, 2 * 60 * 9.80665e3                            # self-weight and maximum Bc load
delta = keta.fasc61_delta(L, G, S)
mx, mn, rmx, rmn = keta.convoy_extreme(line, keta.fasc61_bc(), 3000)
print(f"Bc (one line of trucks): M = {mn / 1e3:.1f} kN.m, head of the convoy at s = {rmn:.2f} m; "
      f"dynamic amplification delta = {delta:.4f}")
mx, mn, rmx, rmn = keta.convoy_extreme(line, keta.fasc61_mc120(), 3000)
print(f"Mc120: M = {mn / 1e3:.1f} kN.m")

# Courbon's transverse distribution: 4 girders, unit load at y = 3 m
K = keta.courbon_coefficients([-4.5, -1.5, 1.5, 4.5], y=3.0)
print("Courbon coefficients:", [round(k, 4) for k in K])
```

Output

```text
maximum ordinate |eta| = 7.5000 m (L/4 = 7.5000 m)
carriageway of 9 m: 3 lanes of 3.0 m, remaining area 0.0 m
lane 1: tandem 300 kN/axle, UDL 27.0 kN/m -> M =   -7357.5 kN.m
lane 2: tandem 200 kN/axle, UDL 7.5 kN/m -> M =   -3723.7 kN.m
lane 3: tandem 100 kN/axle, UDL 7.5 kN/m -> M =   -2283.7 kN.m
A(l): loaded length 30.00 m, A(30) = 10661.2 N/m2 -> M = -8395.7 kN.m
Bc (one line of trucks): M = -2868.4 kN.m, head of the convoy at s = 8.84 m; dynamic amplification delta = 1.0940
Mc120: M = -7268.0 kN.m
Courbon coefficients: [-0.05, 0.15, 0.35, 0.55]
```

## 12.6 Transverse distribution

Syntax

```python
keta.courbon_coefficients(girder_y, weights=[], y)  →  [K1, K2, …]
keta.separable_surface(line, ky, k)  →  InfluenceSurface
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `girder_y` | m | — | transverse positions of the girders |
| `weights` | — | [] | relative second moments of area of the girders (empty: identical girders) |
| `y` | m | — | transverse position of the unit load |
| `line` | — | — | longitudinal influence line |
| `ky, k` | m; — | — | transverse positions and distribution coefficients K(y): the surface is η(x)·K(y) |

Courbon's method (infinitely stiff cross-beams) gives the share of a load carried by each girder.
`separable_surface` builds an influence surface from an influence line and a transverse
distribution law, for a simplified grillage analysis.

## 12.7 Influence surfaces

Syntax

```python
m.influence_surface(nodes, nx, ny, response, dir=(0, 0, -1))  →  InfluenceSurface
m.influence_surface_cloud(nodes, response, dir=(0, 0, -1))  →  CloudSurface
m.lm1_surface(nodes, nx, ny, response, y0, y1, minimise=False, step_y=0.05, factors='class1')  →  dict
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nodes` | — | — | deck nodes; for a grid, list ordered by successive rows (x increasing then y increasing), nx × ny nodes |
| `nx, ny` | — | — | numbers of grid nodes along x and y |
| `response` | — | — | response studied (Table 12.1, without 'bar_displacement') |
| `dir` | — | (0, 0, −1) | direction of the unit load |
| `y0, y1` | m | — | edges of the carriageway (y ordinates) |
| `minimise` | — | False | search for the minimum instead of the maximum |
| `step_y` | m | 0.05 | transverse sweep step of the lanes |

The influence surface on a grid is interpolated bilinearly between the nodes; the one on a cloud
of nodes (skew deck, fan-shaped deck) is linear on a Delaunay triangulation of the positions in plan.
Their placement methods are:

| Method (InfluenceSurface) | Result |
|---|---|
| `x`, `y`, `eta` | coordinates of the grid and ordinates by rows |
| `at(x, y)`, `integral()`, `integral_pos()`, `integral_neg()`, `integral_box(x0, x1, y0, y1)` | ordinate, total integrals, by sign, over a rectangle |
| `point_extreme()` | (max, min) under a unit load |
| `udl_extreme(p)` | surface load p on the favourable zones: dict(max, min, at_max, at_min) |
| `patch_extreme(a, b, p, steps_x=60, steps_y=60)` | rectangle a × b loaded at p, moved over the grid |
| `wheel_set_extreme(wheels, steps_x=60, steps_y=60)`, `wheel_set_value(wheels, rx, ry)` | wheel set [(dx, dy, P)] moved over the grid; value at one position |
| `vehicle_extreme(wheels, y0, y1, both_directions=True, minimise=False)` | exact extreme of a vehicle whose wheels remain within [y0, y1]: dict(value, x, y, reversed) |
| `load_group(group, y0, y1, minimise=False, factors='class1', footways=[], vehicle=[], clear=0.0, step_y=0.05, concomitant=[])` | group of loads of EN 1991-2: 'gr1a' (LM1 and footways at 3 kN/m²), 'gr4' (crowd 5 kN/m²), 'gr5' (special vehicle and frequent LM1); dict(value, lm1, footways, vehicle, vehicle_at, concomitant) |

`CloudSurface` has `at`, `integral`, `integral_pos`,
`integral_neg`, `wheels_value(wheels, rx, ry)` and
`wheels_extreme(wheels, steps_x, steps_y)`. `lm1_surface` places the complete
model 1 (lanes, tandems and distributed loads on the unfavourable zones) and returns
dict(value, remaining, lanes), each lane being described by its rank, its edge
`y_start`, the position `ts_x` of its tandem and its loads.

Example `examples/manual/ex_surface_influence.py`

```python
# Influence surfaces: grillage of 24 m x 9 m (5 main girders, cross-beams),
# deflection and reaction; full LM1, load groups, special vehicle and wheel set.
import keta

nx, ny, Lx, Ly = 13, 7, 24.0, 9.0
m = keta.Model()
concrete = m.concrete()
g = [[m.add_node(Lx * i / (nx - 1), Ly * j / (ny - 1), 0.0) for i in range(nx)] for j in range(ny)]
girder = m.add_section_props(sx=0.9, iy=0.35, iz=0.05, ix=0.02)     # longitudinal girders
xbeam = m.add_section_props(sx=0.3, iy=0.02, iz=0.01, ix=0.005)     # cross-beams / slab
for j in range(ny):
    for i in range(nx - 1):
        m.add_beam(g[j][i], g[j][i + 1], girder if j % 3 == 0 else xbeam, concrete)
for i in range(nx):
    for j in range(ny - 1):
        m.add_beam(g[j][i], g[j + 1][i], xbeam, concrete)
for j in range(ny):
    m.add_support(g[j][0], dx=(j == 0), dy=(j == 0), dz=True)
    m.add_support(g[j][-1], dz=True)
nodes = [nd for row in g for nd in row]                        # successive rows (order x then y)
centre = g[ny // 2][nx // 2]

srf = m.influence_surface(nodes, nx, ny, dict(kind="displacement", node=centre, comp=2))
print(f"grid {len(srf.x)} x {len(srf.y)}; ordinate at the centre {srf.at(12.0, 4.5) * 1e9:.4f} mm/MN")
print(f"deflection under 1 kN/m2: everywhere {srf.integral() * 1e6:.4f} mm, unfavourable zones "
      f"{srf.integral_neg() * 1e6:.4f} mm, rectangle [8;16]x[3;6] {srf.integral_box(8, 16, 3, 6) * 1e6:.4f} mm")
mx, mn = srf.point_extreme()
print(f"unit point load: min {mn * 1e9:.4f} mm/MN")
u = srf.udl_extreme(5e3)
print(f"distributed load of 5 kN/m2 on the unfavourable zones: {u['min'] * 1e3:.4f} mm")
lm = m.lm1_surface(nodes, nx, ny, dict(kind="displacement", node=centre, comp=2), 0.0, 9.0, minimise=True)
print(f"LM1: extreme deflection {lm['value'] * 1e3:.3f} mm; lanes:")
for v in lm["lanes"]:
    print(f"   lane {v['rank']}: edge y = {v['y_start']:.2f} m, tandem at x = {v['ts_x']:.2f} m")
gr1a = srf.load_group("gr1a", 0.0, 9.0, minimise=True)
gr4 = srf.load_group("gr4", 0.0, 9.0, minimise=True)
print(f"group gr1a: {gr1a['value'] * 1e3:.3f} mm; group gr4 (crowd): {gr4['value'] * 1e3:.3f} mm")
wheels = keta.annex_a_vehicle("1800/200", [(-1.0, 0.5), (1.0, 0.5)])  # 2 lines of wheels at +/- 1 m
v = srf.vehicle_extreme(wheels, y0=0.0, y1=9.0, minimise=True)
print(f"special vehicle 1800/200 ({len(wheels)} wheels): {v['value'] * 1e3:.3f} mm at x = {v['x']:.2f}, y = {v['y']:.2f}")
lm2 = keta.lm2_wheels()
print(f"LM2 ({lm2}): {srf.wheel_set_extreme(lm2, 48, 36)['min'] * 1e3:.3f} mm")

# Support reaction on an arbitrary cloud of nodes (triangulation of the positions in plan)
cloud = m.influence_surface_cloud(nodes, dict(kind="reaction", node=g[0][0], comp=2))
print(f"surface on a cloud: corner reaction for 100 kN at (2, 1) m = {cloud.wheels_value([(0, 0, 100e3)], 2.0, 1.0) / 1e3:.3f} kN")
```

Output

```text
grid 13 x 7; ordinate at the centre -9.2533 mm/MN
deflection under 1 kN/m2: everywhere -1.1061 mm, unfavourable zones -1.1061 mm, rectangle [8;16]x[3;6] -0.2037 mm
unit point load: min -9.2533 mm/MN
distributed load of 5 kN/m2 on the unfavourable zones: -5.5307 mm
LM1: extreme deflection -15.367 mm; lanes:
   lane 1: edge y = 3.00 m, tandem at x = 12.00 m
   lane 2: edge y = 6.00 m, tandem at x = 12.00 m
   lane 3: edge y = 0.00 m, tandem at x = 12.00 m
group gr1a: -15.367 mm; group gr4 (crowd): -5.531 mm
special vehicle 1800/200 (18 wheels): -13.775 mm at x = 6.00, y = 5.00
LM2 ([[0.0, -1.0, 200000.0], [0.0, 1.0, 200000.0]]): -3.599 mm
surface on a cloud: corner reaction for 100 kN at (2, 1) m = 55.181 kN
```

## 12.8 Railway loads

Syntax

```python
keta.rail_lm71(alpha=1.0)  →  convoy
keta.rail_sw0(alpha=1.0)  →  convoy
keta.rail_sw2()  →  convoy
keta.rail_hslm_b(n_axles, spacing)  →  convoy
keta.rail_unloaded_train()  →  N/m
keta.rail_phi2(L_phi), keta.rail_phi3(L_phi)  →  dynamic factors
keta.rail_traction(loaded_length, alpha=1.0), keta.rail_braking(loaded_length, model='LM71', alpha=1.0)  →  N
keta.rail_nosing(alpha=1.0)  →  N
keta.rail_centrifugal_factor(v_kmh, L_f), keta.rail_centrifugal_force(v_kmh, radius, q_vertical, L_f)
keta.eccentric_rail(total, ratio=1.25, gauge=1.5)  →  (Q1, Q2, e)
keta.ballast_patches(axle_load, depth=0.3, sleeper='monobloc', three_sleepers=True, spacing=0.6)
keta.annex_d_train(number)  →  dict ;  keta.annex_d_mix(mix)  →  [(train, trains per day, Mt/year)]
keta.rail_n0_lower(L_phi), keta.rail_fatigue_dynamic_factor(v_ms, L_phi, n0)
```

These functions give the load models LM71, SW/0, SW/2 and “unloaded train”, the HSLM-B train
(`n_axles` forces of 170 kN spaced at `spacing`; the number of forces and the
spacing are read on Figures 6.12 and 6.13 of EN 1991-2 according to the span), the dynamic factors
Φ2 and Φ3, the traction, braking, nosing and centrifugal forces, the eccentric distribution of the
loads on the rails, the distribution of axle loads through the ballast, the service trains of
Annex D and their mixes, the lower limit of the first natural frequency and the fatigue dynamic
factor. The dynamic behaviour under high-speed trains and the track-bridge interaction are treated
by:

Syntax

```python
m.rail_speed_sweep(path, train, speeds, observe, zeta=0.02, n_modes=10, free_time=0.0,
                   steps_per_period=20, max_travel=0.5)  →  dict
keta.track_bridge_uic774(decks, rail_A, rail_I, rail_dT, k_unloaded, r_unloaded, k_loaded, r_loaded,
                         train, element=2.0, emb_left=300.0, emb_right=300.0, rail_E=210e9,
                         rail_alpha=1.2e-5, steps=10)  →  dict
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | — | — | bars of the running path |
| `train` | — | — | 'hslm_a1' to 'hslm_a10', list of axles [(offset ≤ 0, load)] or suspended axles [dict(offset, m_wheel, m_body, k, c)] (vehicle-bridge interaction) |
| `speeds` | m/s | — | speeds studied |
| `observe` | — | — | list of observed (node, component) pairs |
| `zeta` | — | 0.02 | modal damping ratio |
| `n_modes` | — | 10 | number of modes of the modal superposition |
| `decks` | — | — | successive decks: dict(length, A, I, E, alpha, e_track, e_bearing, k_left, k_right, dT) |
| `rail_A, rail_I` | m², m⁴ | — | area and second moment of area of the rails |
| `rail_dT` | K | — | temperature variation of the rails |
| `k_unloaded, r_unloaded, k_loaded, r_loaded` | N/m², N/m | — | stiffnesses and limit forces of the longitudinal resistance of the track, unloaded and loaded |
| `train (UIC 774-3)` | — | — | dict(length, horizontal, vertical, forward, front_first, front_last, positions): length, horizontal and vertical loads per metre, direction, extreme positions of the head and number of positions |

`rail_speed_sweep` computes, by superposition on the first `n_modes` modes
(exact modal forces of the moving axles, each oscillator advanced step by step under a load linear
over the step; Newmark scheme for sprung axles), the envelopes of the displacements and accelerations of the observed points for each speed, the static
envelope, the dynamic amplification factor and the critical speed. The result is a dictionary
`points` (one entry per speed: speed, u_max, u_min, a_max),
`static_max`, `static_min`, `dynamic_factor`, `critical_speed`.
`track_bridge_uic774` applies the method of UIC leaflet 774-3: thermal state, then
successive positions of the train, and returns for each state (thermal, positions, envelope) the
extreme stresses of the rail, the forces on the bearings and the relative displacements.

Example `examples/manual/ex_ferroviaire.py`

```python
# Railway actions: dynamic factors, horizontal forces, speed sweep
# under HSLM-A1 of a 20 m span and track-bridge interaction.
import keta

Lphi = 20.0
print(f"dynamic factors: phi2 = {keta.rail_phi2(Lphi):.4f}, phi3 = {keta.rail_phi3(Lphi):.4f}")
print(f"traction {keta.rail_traction(Lphi) / 1e3:.0f} kN, LM71 braking {keta.rail_braking(Lphi) / 1e3:.0f} kN, "
      f"nosing {keta.rail_nosing() / 1e3:.0f} kN")
print(f"centrifugal: f = {keta.rail_centrifugal_factor(160, Lphi):.4f}, "
      f"Qtk = {keta.rail_centrifugal_force(160, 1500, 250e3, Lphi) / 1e3:.3f} kN per axle of 250 kN")
q1, q2, e = keta.eccentric_rail(250e3)
print(f"load eccentricity: {q1 / 1e3:.2f} / {q2 / 1e3:.2f} kN, e = {e:.4f} m")

# Simply supported span of 20 m, 20 bars, mass 8000 kg/m3 x 1 m2
m = keta.Model()
nd = [m.add_node(float(i), 0, 0) for i in range(21)]
sec = m.add_section_props(sx=1.0, iy=0.04, iz=0.04, ix=0.08)
mat = m.add_material(e=2.0e11, nu=0.3, rho=8000.0)
bars = [m.add_beam(nd[i], nd[i + 1], sec, mat) for i in range(20)]
for i, x in enumerate(nd):
    m.add_support(x, dx=(i == 0), dy=True, dz=(i in (0, 20)), rx=True, rz=True)
f1 = m.modal(n_modes=1).frequencies[0]
print(f"first frequency {f1:.3f} Hz; lower limit n0 = {keta.rail_n0_lower(Lphi):.3f} Hz")
speeds = [40.0 + 5.0 * i for i in range(9)]
sweep = m.rail_speed_sweep(bars, "hslm_a1", speeds, [(nd[10], 2)], zeta=0.02, n_modes=4)
for p in sweep["points"]:
    print(f"  v = {p['speed']:5.1f} m/s: min deflection {p['u_min'][0] * 1e3:8.3f} mm, "
          f"max acceleration {p['a_max'][0]:7.3f} m/s2")
print(f"static {sweep['static_min'][0] * 1e3:.3f} mm; dynamic amplification {sweep['dynamic_factor'][0]:.4f}; "
      f"critical speed {sweep['critical_speed'][0]:.1f} m/s")

# Track-bridge interaction (UIC 774-3): deck of 60 m, fixed bearing on the left
deck = dict(length=60, A=0.74, I=2.59, e_track=1.21, e_bearing=4.79, k_left=6e8, dT=35)
u = keta.track_bridge_uic774([deck], rail_A=0.01534126, rail_I=6.07756e-5, rail_dT=50,
                             k_unloaded=1e7, r_unloaded=2e4, k_loaded=3e7, r_loaded=6e4,
                             train=dict(front_first=300, front_last=450, positions=2))
print(f"UIC 774-3, thermal state: rail stress {u['thermal']['rail_min'] / 1e6:.2f} MPa, "
      f"force on the fixed bearing {u['thermal']['bearing'][0] / 1e3:.1f} kN")
print(f"envelope: rail stress {u['envelope']['rail_min'] / 1e6:.2f} MPa, "
      f"force on the fixed bearing {u['envelope']['bearing'][0] / 1e3:.1f} kN")
```

Output

```text

traction 660 kN, LM71 braking 400 kN, nosing 100 kN
centrifugal: f = 0.8303, Qtk = 27.894 kN per axle of 250 kN
load eccentricity: 111.11 / 138.89 kN, e = 0.0833 m
first frequency 3.925 Hz; lower limit n0 = 4.000 Hz
  v =  40.0 m/s: min deflection  -15.417 mm, max acceleration   2.110 m/s2
  v =  45.0 m/s: min deflection  -14.642 mm, max acceleration   2.086 m/s2
```

The resonance of the 20 m span occurs at 70 m/s: the first natural frequency (3.925 Hz)
multiplied by the length of the coaches of the HSLM-A1 train (18 m) gives 70.7 m/s.

## 12.9 Fatigue

Syntax

```python
keta.convoy_history(line, convoy, exact=True, steps=500)  →  (positions, effects)
keta.turning_points(series)  →  [values]
keta.rainflow(series)  →  [(range, mean, count), …]
```

`convoy_history` gives the history of the effect of a convoy crossing the influence
line. With `exact=True`, the effect is computed at each position where an axle or an
end of a distributed load passes over a point of the line: for a piecewise linear line
(`from_samples`) and axles only, the effect is linear between these positions, which
therefore contain its extremes; for a line computed on the model (cubic between its points) or a
convoy with distributed loads, 8 intermediate positions are added per interval. With
`exact=False`, the effect is computed at `steps` + 1 regular positions. `turning_points` extracts the turning points of a series and
`rainflow` performs the cycle counting on it by the rainflow method (ASTM E1049): each
cycle is counted as 1 or 0.5. The damage is then computed in Python by Miner's rule with the
desired resistance curve.

Example `examples/manual/ex_fatigue.py`

```python
# Fatigue: history of the midspan moment of a continuous beam 2 x 20 m under the passage
# of the FLM3 vehicle, rainflow counting and Miner damage (curve of slope m = 3).
import keta

m = keta.Model()
n = [m.add_node(2.0 * i, 0, 0) for i in range(21)]
b = [m.add_beam(n[i], n[i + 1], m.add_section_props(0.5, 0.08, 0.5, 0.05), m.steel()) for i in range(20)]
m.add_support(n[0], dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
m.add_support(n[10], dy=True, dz=True)
m.add_support(n[20], dy=True, dz=True)
line = m.influence_line(b, dict(kind="bar_force", bar=b[4], x=2.0, comp=4))  # My at x = 10 m

flm3 = keta.flm3_vehicle()
print("FLM3:", [(d, round(p / 1e3)) for d, p in flm3["axles"]], "(offset m, kN)")
r, M = keta.convoy_history(line, flm3)
print(f"history: {len(M)} positions, M from {min(M) / 1e3:.1f} to {max(M) / 1e3:.1f} kN.m")
tp = keta.turning_points(M)
print("turning points [kN.m]:", [round(x / 1e3, 1) for x in tp])
cycles = keta.rainflow(M)
for range_, mean, count in cycles:
    print(f"   cycle: range {range_ / 1e3:8.2f} kN.m, mean {mean / 1e3:8.2f} kN.m, count {count}")

W = 0.08 / 0.5                                   # section modulus I / v [m3]
dsc, NC = 71e6, 2e6                              # detail category 71 MPa at 2e6 cycles
D = sum(nb * ((e / W) / dsc) ** 3 / NC for e, _, nb in cycles)
print(f"damage of one passage: {D:.3e}; allowable passages: {1 / D:.3e}")
```

Output

```text
FLM3: [(0.0, 120), (1.2, 120), (7.2, 120), (8.4, 120)] (offset m, kN)
history: 2179 positions, M from -1209.4 to 394.4 kN.m
turning points [kN.m]: [0.0, -1209.4, -1141.6, -1163.5, 394.4, 0.0]
   cycle: range    21.90 kN.m, mean -1152.52 kN.m, count 1.0
   cycle: range  1209.41 kN.m, mean  -604.70 kN.m, count 0.5
   cycle: range  1603.83 kN.m, mean  -407.49 kN.m, count 0.5
   cycle: range   394.43 kN.m, mean   197.21 kN.m, count 0.5
damage of one passage: 1.016e-09; allowable passages: 9.846e+08
```

# Chapter 13 Staged construction

## 13.1 Principle

The staged construction analysis follows the construction of a structure: the structure evolves
(bars cast or erected, temporary supports, closures, stressing operations, dismantling) and the
loads apply to the structure present at the time they act. Between two dates, the concrete creeps
and shrinks and the tendons lose part of their force.

**Figure 13.1** — A staged construction: the structure changes from one stage to the next, its states add up

keta performs this analysis by incremental superposition. The stages are run through in the order
of their dates; each event (activation, loading, stressing, support removal, creep increment) is
computed linearly on the substructure active at that instant, and its effect is added to the state
reached. The forces “locked” into the structure by the construction history are thus preserved. In
particular:

- an activated bar is born stress-free in the current deformed geometry;

- a deactivated bar or a removed support returns to the remaining structure the forces it
carried;

- the loads of a case applied in a stage remain applied in the following stages;

- between two dates, each concrete bar with a time-dependent law (Chapter 7) receives the creep
strain increment of its stress history (Boltzmann superposition) and the shrinkage increment;
the tendons undergo the coupled time-dependent losses (shrinkage, creep, relaxation).

## 13.2 Staged construction analysis

Syntax

```python
m.phased(phases, creep_engine='exact', stations=11, exact_losses=True, modulus=None,
         creep_substeps_per_decade=4, creep_along_bar=False, origin_ledgers=False,
         keep_structures=False)  →  Phased
```

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `phases` | — | — | list of stage dictionaries, in chronological order (Section 13.3) |
| `creep_engine` | — | 'exact' | creep calculation method: 'exact' (Boltzmann superposition with the law itself), 'kelvin' (Kelvin chains fitted to the law, one per loading event), 'aaem' (one step per interval: Δε = φ(t₂, t₁)·σ/E, without ageing coefficient; splitting an interval overstates the total creep), 'incremental' (incremental method by fibres) |
| `modulus` | — | None | function f(bar, age in days) → instantaneous modulus [Pa] of each increment, at the age of the concrete of the bar at the date of the stage (bars with a concrete law); None: modulus of the material |
| `stations` | — | 11 | output sections per bar |
| `exact_losses` | — | True | losses of bonded tendons computed through the structure (otherwise section formula of EN 1992-1-1 clause 5.10.6 per interval) |
| `creep_substeps_per_decade` | — | 4 | time substeps per decade of elapsed time within a creep interval |
| `creep_along_bar` | — | False | creep computed at each output section (otherwise one mean stress per bar, taken at mid-length) |
| `origin_ledgers` | — | False | storage of the cumulative state broken down by origin (loads, prestressing, losses) |
| `keep_structures` | — | False | storage of the active substructure of each stage, read by `PhaseResult.tangent()` (Section 16.7) |

**Important.**

With the default options, the creep of a bar is computed from the stress at mid-length and
applied as a uniform strain: the approximation is valid only for bars that are short compared with
the variation of the forces. For an accurate redistribution (closure, continuity),
`creep_along_bar=True` is activated and `creep_substeps_per_decade` is
increased (example of Section 13.6).

## 13.3 Description of the stages

Each stage is a dictionary whose keys are the following; only the useful keys are given. An
unknown key raises `ValueError`.

Table 13.1 — Keys of a stage

| Key | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | name of the stage (default “phase i”) |
| `time` | days | date of the stage; creep acts between the dates |
| `activate` | [bars] | activated bars (cast or erected stress-free); bars never cited are active from the start |
| `activate_age` | {bar: age} | concrete age [days] of the activated bars (default 0: concrete cast at the date of the stage) |
| `deactivate` | [bars] | bars removed, forces returned |
| `add_supports` | [dict(node, dx, dy, dz, rx, ry, rz)] | supports added (by default translations restrained, rotations free) |
| `remove_supports` | [nodes] | supports removed, reactions returned |
| `cases` | [cases] | load cases applied from this stage onwards |
| `tension` | [dict(tendon, fraction, mode, unbonded, group)] | stressing and destressing of tendons (Section 8.2) |
| `inject` | [tendons] | grouting of the stressed ungrouted tendons |
| `inject_partial` | [(tendon, s0, s1)] | partial grouting between two abscissae |
| `place_hinges`, `close_hinges` | [dict(bar, end=1, dofs='rz')] | placing of a temporary hinge at one end of a bar (end 0: origin, 1: end; dofs: local components released, for example 'ry'); closure of the hinge |
| `modify_sections` | [(bar, section)] | change of section of an active bar (without time-dependent material) |
| `regime` | 'linear' or 'second_order' | regime of the increments of the stage; at second order, equilibrium accounts for the total axial force |
| `imperfection` | [(node, (6 values))] | injected geometric imperfection (acts at second order) |
| `cable_actions` | [dict(cable, kind, value)] | actions on catenary cables: 'length' (unstrained length), 'horizontal' (target horizontal tension), 'end_tension', 'thermal' (relative elongation α·ΔT), 'rupture' (dynamic factor) |

**Note.**

A hinge placed by `place_hinges` is admitted only where the corresponding force is
zero: it is placed before the bar is loaded. The closure `close_hinges` locks the relative
rotation acquired, without force.

## 13.4 Results

The `Phased` object contains one state per stage:

Syntax

```python
len(r)  →  int
r.names()  →  [names of the stages]
r.phase(i)  →  PhaseResult
```

The state of the stage of index i (0 for the first) has the following attributes and methods:

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| `name`, `time` | name and date of the stage |
| `displacement(node)` | cumulative displacement at the end of the stage |
| `increment_displacement(node)` | displacement increment of the stage |
| `bar_forces(bar)` | cumulative forces at the output sections (x/L, N, Vy, Vz, T, My, Mz) |
| `increment_bar_forces(bar)` | force increment of the stage |
| `reactions()` | cumulative reactions |
| `tendons()` | tendons: (id, stressing force, cumulative losses, effective force) |
| `cables()` | catenary cables: (bar, active, L0, H, T1, T2) |

**Note.**

A removed support no longer carries a reaction: from the stage of its removal, it appears
in `reactions()` with a zero reaction, its previous reaction having been returned
to the structure.

## 13.5 Example: beam cast on a prop

A 12 m beam is cast on a central prop, then the prop is removed. The material has no
time-dependent law: the staged construction analysis is purely elastic.

Example `examples/manual/ex_phasage_etai.py`

```python
# Staged construction without creep: beam of 2 x 6 m cast on a central prop, then the prop is removed;
# activations, addition and removal of a support, accumulation of the states.
import keta

L, q = 6.0, -25e3
m = keta.Model()
mat = m.add_material(e=30e9, nu=0.2, rho=0.0)        # no time-dependent law: elastic staging
sec = m.add_section_props(sx=0.3, iy=6.4e-3, iz=2e-3, ix=2e-3)
n = [m.add_node(L * i / 2, 0, 0) for i in range(5)]
b = [m.add_beam(n[i], n[i + 1], sec, mat) for i in range(4)]
m.add_support(n[0], dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
m.add_support(n[4], dy=True, dz=True)
for bi in b:
    m.add_udl(bi, wz=q, case=1)                      # weight of the fresh concrete

r = m.phased([
    dict(name="propping", time=0, activate=b, add_supports=[dict(node=n[2], dx=False, dy=True, dz=True)]),
    dict(name="casting", time=1, cases=[1]),
    dict(name="prop removal", time=28, remove_supports=[n[2]]),
])
for i in range(len(r)):
    p = r.phase(i)
    M = p.bar_forces(b[1])[-1][5]                    # section at mid-length
    R = dict(p.reactions())[n[0]][2]                 # end support
    dM = p.increment_bar_forces(b[1])[-1][5]
    print(f"{p.name:13}: M(mid) = {M / 1e3:8.2f} kN.m (increment {dM / 1e3:8.2f}), "
          f"end reaction = {R / 1e3:7.2f} kN, deflection = {p.displacement(n[2])[2] * 1e3:7.3f} mm")
print(f"on the prop (2 spans of 6 m): M = -q L²/8 = {-q * L * L / 8 / 1e3:.2f} kN.m, R = 3 q L/8 = {-3 * q * L / 8 / 1e3:.2f} kN")
print(f"after prop removal (12 m):   M = q (2L)²/8 = {q * (2 * L)**2 / 8 / 1e3:.2f} kN.m, R = q L = {-q * L / 1e3:.2f} kN")
```

Output

```text
propping     : M(mid) =     0.00 kN.m (increment     0.00), end reaction =    0.00 kN, deflection =   0.000 mm
casting      : M(mid) =   112.50 kN.m (increment   112.50), end reaction =   56.25 kN, deflection =   0.000 mm
prop removal : M(mid) =  -450.00 kN.m (increment  -562.50), end reaction =  150.00 kN, deflection = -35.156 mm
on the prop (2 spans of 6 m): M = -q L²/8 = 112.50 kN.m, R = 3 q L/8 = 56.25 kN
after prop removal (12 m):   M = q (2L)²/8 = -450.00 kN.m, R = q L = 150.00 kN
```

At casting, the beam behaves as a two-span continuous beam; at the removal of the prop, the
reaction of the prop (187.5 kN) is returned to the 12 m beam, whose final state is that of a
statically determinate beam cast in one piece.

## 13.6 Example: closure of two spans

Two precast spans of 20 m are placed on their supports at 20 days, with a hinge over the central
support; they receive their permanent load at 28 days and are then made continuous by a closure at
60 days. Creep (Courbon non-ageing law, φ∞ = 2) gives rise over the support to a continuity moment,
whose limit value is known:
M∞ = Mc (φ∞ − φ(t₁ − t₀)) / (1 + φ∞), Mc being the moment of the beam cast continuous.

Example `examples/manual/ex_phasage_clavage.py`

```python
# Staged construction: two precast spans of 20 m placed as simply supported, then made continuous
# by a closure over the central support; creep redistribution of the support moment.
import math
import keta

L, q, E = 20.0, -50e3, 35e9
m = keta.Model()
concrete = m.add_material(e=E, nu=0.2, rho=0.0)
m.set_concrete_law(concrete, "COURBON", e_direct=E)   # non-ageing creep, phi(inf) = 2
sec = m.add_section_props(sx=0.8, iy=0.25, iz=0.1, ix=0.1)   # rigid in shear
n = [m.add_node(L * i / 4, 0, 0) for i in range(9)]
b = [m.add_beam(n[i], n[i + 1], sec, concrete) for i in range(8)]
m.add_support(n[0], dx=True, dy=True, dz=True, rx=True)
m.add_support(n[4], dy=True, dz=True)
m.add_support(n[8], dy=True, dz=True)
for bi in b:
    m.add_udl(bi, wz=q, case=1)                    # self-weight + superimposed dead loads

phases = [
    dict(name="placing", time=20, place_hinges=[dict(bar=b[3], end=1, dofs="ry")]),
    dict(name="loading", time=28, cases=[1]),
    dict(name="closure", time=60, close_hinges=[dict(bar=b[3], end=1, dofs="ry")]),
    dict(name="1 year", time=393),
    dict(name="30 years", time=28 + 30 * 365),
]
r = m.phased(phases, creep_along_bar=True, creep_substeps_per_decade=32)
print("stages:", r.names())
for i in range(len(r)):
    p = r.phase(i)
    Ma = p.bar_forces(b[3])[-1][5] + 0.0         # moment at the end of the bar over the support
    print(f"{p.name:11} t = {p.time:6.0f} days: M(support) = {abs(Ma) / 1e3:8.2f} kN.m, "
          f"midspan deflection = {p.displacement(n[2])[2] * 1e3:8.3f} mm")
r0 = m.phased(phases)                            # default options: creep at mid-bar
print(f"default options, 30 years: M(support) = {r0.phase(4).bar_forces(b[3])[-1][5] / 1e3:.2f} kN.m")

# Check: non-ageing law, exact limit M = Mc (phi(inf) - phi(t1 - t0)) / (1 + phi(inf))
phi = lambda d: 2 * (1 - math.exp(-0.006 * d))
Mc = -q * L * L / 8                              # moment of the beam cast continuous
M30 = Mc * (phi(30 * 365) - phi(60 - 28)) / (1 + phi(30 * 365))
print(f"beam cast continuous: Mc = {Mc / 1e3:.2f} kN.m; limit by creep: {M30 / 1e3:.2f} kN.m")
```

Output

```text
stages: ['placing', 'loading', 'closure', '1 year', '30 years']
placing     t =     20 days: M(support) =     0.00 kN.m, midspan deflection =    0.000 mm
loading     t =     28 days: M(support) =     0.00 kN.m, midspan deflection =  -11.905 mm
closure     t =     60 days: M(support) =     0.00 kN.m, midspan deflection =  -16.062 mm
1 year      t =    393 days: M(support) =  1372.57 kN.m, midspan deflection =  -22.854 mm
30 years    t =  10978 days: M(support) =  1374.65 kN.m, midspan deflection =  -23.920 mm
default options, 30 years: M(support) = 1437.01 kN.m
beam cast continuous: Mc = 2500.00 kN.m; limit by creep: 1375.51 kN.m
```
